title: “Rename with PowerRename” Will Not Replace the U+2014 (—) EM DASH with the Two-Character Substring U+A789 (꞉) MODIFIER LETTER COLON Just Before a U+0020 ( ) SPACE (That Is, “꞉ ”) in File or Folder Names
summary: PowerRename preview-versus-disk mismatch needs a literal/regex control, not a presumed Unicode fix.

evidence: The current body identifies PowerToys 0.102.3001, Windows 11 build 26300.9711, administrator mode, and a seven-step replacement of U+2014 with U+A789 followed by U+0020. Preview changes but Explorer names reportedly do not.

The supplied report predates that current version claim: its PowerRename entries are from 0.102.2933 and retain a digit/dash/letter regular expression with capture-group replacement, not the literal-only search in the body.
The saved flags enable regular expressions as well as enumeration. The inspected PowerRename log entries do not identify a failed shell-operation result.
Read the complete current body, automation comment and attached report; checked the persisted pattern, replacement, flags and PowerRename logs rather than relying on the automation subset.
PowerRenameManager.cpp::_PerformFileOperation queues RenameItem, may update the in-memory name before execution when the window stays open, and does not check the PerformOperations result.

Focused manager history contains no recent apply-result correction. Related PR #51297 addresses linguistically equal names and a disabled preview/Apply state, unlike this report of successful preview followed by failed filesystem change; it is not established coverage.

The issue timeline and bounded upstream/fork searches identify no covering implementation or assigned owner. The existing conditional investigation is retained, not replaced by a claimed Unicode root cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the supplied synthetic controls and resolve the one saved-state discrepancy before selecting an apply-result fix.
judgment.rationale: The detailed steps support maintainer reproduction, but the archived mode differs from the body and no failed shell result is established.

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional apply-result correction remains plausible; no concrete PR is established as covering this behavior.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: shell execution may fail after preview and optimistic in-memory updates. The report does not yet distinguish that path from the saved regex-state discrepancy; U+A789 is not established as the cause.

verification: Compare on-disk filenames with preview after literal and regex substitutions, including a cancelled or failed shell rename.
Verify trailing space is internal to the name and that unchanged files are not reported as renamed.

plan: Reproduce the literal and archived regex cases independently.
If shell execution fails, trace queue and completion results before designing a success-only UI/state update.
Preserve partial-success and Undo behavior and add a regression case for the confirmed failure.

comment.body: Thanks for the precise code points, steps and attached report. The current body says 0.102.3001, while the attached PowerRename state is from 0.102.2933 and saves a regex/capture-group replacement. Please share one non-sensitive failing filename with its expected and actual names on 0.102.3001, and confirm whether regular expressions is enabled for that attempt. This distinguishes the saved-state discrepancy from a shell apply failure; another general log bundle is not needed first.

reproduce.expected_result: Successful operations produce the previewed names on disk; failed/cancelled operations do not leave optimistic success state.
setup: Create test files named A—B.txt and 1—A.txt in a writable test folder; enable PowerRename.
prerequisites: Use non-sensitive test data and preserve the original configuration before changing it.
steps: 1. Select both files and open PowerRename; choose Filename only.
2. With regex off, replace U+2014 with U+A789 followed by U+0020; compare preview and disk after Apply.
3. Reset the names; enable regex and use (\d)—([A-Za-z]) with replacement $1꞉ $2.
4. Record per-file shell completion and whether the UI claims success before execution; do not treat a completion trace as proof of a disk rename.
reproduce.title: Verify the reported PowerRename transition
